preconditions.description: The input contains at least one line (the number of test cases T).

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(line, str) for line in stdin.strip().splitlines())
preconditions.description: All lines in the input are strings.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in '#.' for c in line) for line in stdin.strip().splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each test case string P consists only of characters '#' and '.'.

preconditions.expression: all(line[0] == '#' and line[-1] == '#' for line in stdin.strip().splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: For every test case string P, the first and last characters are '#', representing floorboards at the start and end.
The integer T on the first line equals the number of subsequent test case lines.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.
Each line of output is a non-negative integer representing the number of days.

postconditions.expression: all(lambda i: int(stdout.strip().splitlines()[i]) == sum(1 for j in range(len(P)) if P[j] == '.' and (j - (max([k for k in range(j) if P[k] == '#'] or [-1])) - 1) > current_max_jump and (current_max_jump := max(current_max_jump, j - (max([k for k in range(j) if P[k] == '#'] or [-1])) - 1))) for i, P in enumerate(stdin.strip().splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: For each test case string P, the output integer equals the number of times the required jump length (distance between consecutive floorboards) exceeds the current maximum jump capability, where the capability updates to the new required length upon each such event, starting from an initial capability of 1.
